<details>
The provided `.SRCINFO` file contains metadata for the `tuios-plot-bin` AUR package. It defines the package base, version, description, architecture support, source URLs, and checksums. The sources point to official GitHub releases under the project's legitimate repository (https://github.com/Gaurav-Gosain/tuios), specifically versioned release assets. The SHA-256 checksums are provided for both `aarch64` and `x86_64` binaries, matching their respective downloadable tarballs.

All URLs are HTTPS-secured and point to the expected upstream project release page. The package does not use `git` sources or dynamic fetching at build time, nor does it execute arbitrary scripts or download content from third-party locations. The use of `::` in the source lines correctly separates the custom filename from the upstream URL, which is standard AUR practice. The `sha256sums` are explicit and not set to 'SKIP', indicating verified integrity.

There is no evidence of obfuscated commands, unauthorized network activity, or execution of unverified code. The package adheres to standard AUR packaging practices and appears to safely distribute a prebuilt binary of an open-source terminal plotting tool.
</details>

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD file defines a standard Arch Linux package build configuration for distributing a prebuilt binary of the `tuios-plot-bin` tool. It fetches release assets from the official GitHub repository `https://github.com/Gaurav-Gosain/tuios/releases`, which matches the declared upstream URL `https://tuios.dev`. The sources are specific to architecture (aarch64 and x86_64), and each has a corresponding SHA-256 checksum provided, ensuring integrity verification during build.

The `package()` function performs straightforward installation tasks: copying the binary to `/usr/bin`, the license to `/usr/share/licenses`, and the README to `/usr/share/doc`. These operations are confined to the package directory (`${pkgdir}`) and follow standard packaging practices. No network operations, dynamic code evaluation, or suspicious commands (e.g., `curl|bash`, `eval`, `base64` decoding) are present.

The package metadata (e.g., license, description, URL) is consistent with the project's stated purpose: a terminal-based plotting tool for CSV, TSV, or JSON. There are no signs of obfuscated code, unexpected file manipulations, or execution of downloaded content. The use of GoReleaser is noted, which is common for Go-based projects, and does not imply malicious intent. All actions are transparent and verifiable.
</details>
